drug_class: Biologic / monoclonal antibody (thymic stromal lymphopoietin, or TSLP, blocker)
purpose: Tezepelumab-ekko is used to help control severe asthma in adults and children 12 years and older. It is an add-on treatment, meaning it works alongside your other asthma medicines to reduce asthma attacks. It can help you breathe better and improve your overall quality of life.
how_it_works: Your body sometimes releases a protein called TSLP that triggers inflammation and makes asthma worse. This medication blocks that protein before it can set off the chain reaction that causes swelling and tightening in your airways. By stopping that trigger early, it helps keep your asthma under better control.
common_side_effects: Sore throat, joint pain, back pain, and reactions at the injection site such as redness, swelling, or mild pain. Some people may also get headaches or feel generally achy.
warnings: Do not use this medicine to treat a sudden asthma attack or severe breathing episode — it will not work fast enough in an emergency. Tell your doctor before starting if you have a parasitic infection. Do not stop your other asthma medicines unless your doctor tells you to. Allergic reactions are possible, so let your doctor or pharmacist know right away if you notice hives, swelling, or difficulty breathing after your injection.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 210 mg given as a shot (injection) under the skin once every 4 weeks. It can be given by a healthcare provider in a clinic, or you may be able to give it to yourself at home after proper training.
